topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the opening framing, introducing the lecture series, the speakers, and the key learning outcomes regarding cancer causation.

topics.label: Genetic, Evolutionary, and Endogenous Drivers of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational concept of cancer as a micro-evolutionary genetic disease driven by endogenous metabolic processes, replication errors, and inherited genetic predispositions.

topics.label: Environmental Exposures and the Etiological Debate
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the controversy over intrinsic random mutations versus extrinsic environmental exposures using global epidemiological data and migration studies.

topics.label: Infectious Pathogens in Cancer Etiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how viral, bacterial, and parasitic infections interact with host immunity and cellular proliferation to drive tumorigenesis, highlighted by the role of EBV and malaria in Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and Physical Mutagenesis and Metabolic Activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular mechanisms by which radiation, dietary toxins, and chemical carcinogens undergo metabolic transformation to induce DNA adducts and oxidative stress.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Inflammation, and Host Susceptibility Factors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address non-mutagenic mechanisms of carcinogenesis, focusing on chronic inflammation, the two-stage model of promotion, and developmental windows of vulnerability.

topics.label: Experimental and Epidemiological Methodologies for Assessing Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the scientific approaches used to detect and prove carcinogenicity, including whole-genome mutational signatures, population biobanks, animal models, and the Ames assay.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Risk-Benefit Considerations
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the closing framing of the lecture, reflecting on daily risk-benefit decisions regarding environmental and lifestyle exposures.
